Board Meeting Recap
 Wayne Local Schools - November 9, 2026
 Welcome! 
 Welcome to our WLS Board of Education Recap. This document provides an overview of the broad topics covered at each board meeting. If you prefer more detail, please access Board Docs at wayne-local.com . 
 We are using a platform that includes translation features in many different languages.  Setting the Standard for Leadership, Positivity, and Work Ethic
 On November 9, before the Board of Education meeting, eight students and four staff members were honored for their contributions to Wayne Local Schools. These individuals lead by example, strengthen our school culture, and help create a supportive, high-performing environment where everyone can feel like they belong. 
 The district recognizes students and staff members who set the standard for leadership, compassion, work ethic, and positivity at WLS twice each school year.
 The following Spartan Recognition Award recipients were recognized and congratulated by district administrators, Student Board of Education representatives, and Board members:

 Public Participation 
 Two community members addressed the Board; one provided information about Waynesville Elementary's Sensory Space and Motor Room and the the other expressed thanks to Director of Operations Ryan Fullenkamp for his leadership of the district's Transportation Department. 
 Public Participation Policy po0169.1 
 Student Board of Education Update 
 Hayden Harrison, Kate Lundy, Walter Shelhamer, and Logan Walker 
 Student Board of Education representatives shared updates on a variety of district-wide activities, student achievements, and upcoming events. At WES, the Fun Run raised an impressive $68,785 toward additional playground equipment, with preschool earning a $1,000 stipend as the winning grade level. Elementary students participated in PBIS activities, kindergarten fire safety lessons, a Touch-a-Truck event, and a visit to Glen Helen to learn about unique animals.
 WMS students continued building a welcoming school environment through Connect activities and enjoyed their fall dance. Student Council hosted Spirit Week, while students and staff celebrated Halloween with creative costumes. On Unity Day, students and staff wore orange to take a stand against bullying. 
 At WHS, the Leo Club welcomed 50 new members, inducted six officers, added eight members to its leadership team, and hosted a successful Halloween Carnival. Athletic Council members attended the Anthony Muñoz Youth Leadership Conference, while 30 freshmen and sophomores volunteered with Family Promise of Warren County to help prepare for the holidays. Gifted and Art Club students visited Pyramid Hill Sculpture Park, and Foreign Language Club and Spanish 4 and 5 students visited El Mesón to explore Hispanic culture. 
 Student BOE Representatives also recognized 2026 Sauerkraut Festival scholarship recipients Aislin Turkelson, Macy Todd, and Autumn Atkins. Christina Hunt, daughter of WHS alumna Carol Ludington Hunt, visited with Athletic Council and Leo Club members to encourage students to pursue their dreams. Warren County Prosecutor David Fornshell spoke with high school students about common youth offenses and how decisions made in just a few minutes can have lasting consequences. 
 Athletic highlights included the Varsity Game Day Cheer team qualifying for Nationals, WHS Football advancing to the third round of the playoffs, and the Boys Cross Country team placing seventh at State. Jake Todd also qualified individually for State, finishing 23rd. Students also highlighted the hosting of the Spartan Spectacular Cheer Competition. 
 Upcoming events included the WHS Theatre production of Radium Girls , the annual canned food drive beginning later this month, and the much-anticipated Thanksgiving break. 
 Superintendent's Report 
 Superintendent's Update
 Radium Girls 
 Dr. Ison reminded the Board of the upcoming WHS Theatre fall production of Radium Girls , with performances scheduled for November 13 and 14 at 7 p.m. and November 15 at 2 p.m. All performances will take place at the Wayne Local Schools Performing Arts Center. Tickets are $10 for students and $12 for adults and may be purchased at the door with cash or card.
 Veterans Day Celebration 
 Dr. Ison thanked WES Principal Anna Garafolo and WMS/WHS Principal Chip Will for organizing the district’s Veterans Day celebration on November 11. He also invited Board members to attend the festivities, which will begin with a Veterans Breakfast at WES, followed by a special Veterans Day program and a car parade through campus. 
 Consent Agenda - Superintendent 
 As is standard at each Board meeting, several personnel recommendations were presented for approval. Dr. Ison also recommended the following items: 
 Approval to Non-Renew the Fall 2026 Pupil Activity Contracts (customary)
 Approval of Ski Club for 2026/27 School Year 
 2027 UCA High School Cheerleading Nationals 
 Second Reading of WLS Bylaws and Policie s - Dr. Ison presented the second reading of proposed changes, additions, and deletions to several Wayne Local Schools bylaws and policies. The proposed revisions were shared with the Board for review. Please visit BoardDocs to see the first reading of changes.
 The Superintendent’s consent agenda items were approved. 
 Dr. Ison also recommended approval of Board Vice President David Hurley as a volunteer for the 2026–27 8th Grade Girls Basketball. The Board approved the supplemental volunteer. recommendation. 
 Consent Agenda - Treasurer 
 Treasurer Carolyn Huber presented the October financial report and recommended acceptance of eight donations totaling $6,748.88. Contributions from the Waynesville Elementary PTO, American Legion Post 615, SAL Squadron Post 615, G&J Pepsi, and Waynesville Soccer Association will support various student programs and activities. Mrs. Huber also presented a $6,000 appropriation amendment.
 In her financial update, Mrs. Huber reported that revenue is trending $447,808 above forecast, while expenditures are $38,146 higher than projected, resulting in a net favorable cash impact of $409,662. Despite this positive variance, the district's projected General Fund year-end cash balance continues to decline, from $8.4 million in FY2026 to $7.1 million in FY2027.
 Mrs. Huber also highlighted rising operational costs. Over the past decade, the cost of a school bus has increased 83%, copy paper 36%, and half-pint chocolate milk more than 100%, illustrating the continued financial pressures facing public schools.

 Board of Education Update 
 Nicole Bouch (Board Member), Richie Bowling (Board Member), Amanda Garrett (Board President) 
 David Hurley (Board Vice President), and Danny Manley (Board Member) 
 Levy Discussion 
 Board members discussed the timing of a potential school levy, weighing the advantages and disadvantages of placing an issue on the May or November ballot. The discussion included voter turnout, community engagement, and strategies for building support. 
 Board President Amanda Garrett shared that staff interest in participating in levy efforts is high. She expressed interest in forming an exploratory committee that would include staff members who can help communicate the district's value to the community. She also emphasized the importance of engaging voters who may be less supportive of a levy, particularly retired residents, through dialogue. 
 Ms. Garrett also discussed the importance of preparing for a potential May ballot issue, noting that the necessary steps would need to be completed by February. The Board would have the flexibility to reconsider the timing before making a final decision.

 December Board Meeting 
 The Board of Education will meet on December 14 , 2026, at 6 p.m. at the WLS Performing Arts Center on the second floor for a regularly scheduled business meeting. Board meetings are open to the public and can provide context to decision-making that affects our schools and community.
